title: ChatGPT writes Pine Script that wont compile because it learned four versions of the language at once
author: person-person12
selftext:
If youve ever asked ChatGPT for a TradingView indicator, pasted it in and got a wall of red errors, the model isnt being lazy. Pine has been through six versions since 2013 and TradingView still hosts the docs for v3 through v6 on the same site, all of them indexed, so anything trained on the web learned **a blend of four languages** that share a name. You get a v4 `study()` call sitting next to v6 syntax, a `transp=` argument that was removed years ago, and the daily timeframe written the old way inside `request.security`.

The second thing that breaks it is how Pine runs. The script doesnt run once, **it runs again from the top on every candle**, and an ordinary variable resets on each pass unless its declared with `var`. A model writing it like Python will try to count touches of a level and get 1 on every candle, and that version compiles fine and draws garbage, so you dont even get an error telling you its wrong.

The fix most ppl land on is pasting the error back in and going round five or six times, and each round fixes one line and drags something else back in from an older version.

That loop is the reason the indicator side of [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) checks every script against the v6 rules before you see it, rewrites whatever fails until it passes, and then hands it over ready to paste into TradingView and saves a copy to your library.
